````text
---
name: morphing
description: Shape morphing and path interpolation animations for transforming between shapes, icons, blobs, and text. Use when creating icon transitions, liquid effects, organic shape animations, or any shape-to-shape transformations.
---

# Morphing

Shape transformation and path interpolation animations.

## Standards Reference

| Standard | Documentation |
|----------|---------------|
| W3C DTCG | designtokens.org |
| SVG SMIL | developer.mozilla.org/SVG/SVG_animation_with_SMIL |
| CSS clip-path | developer.mozilla.org/CSS/clip-path |
| Flubber | github.com/veltman/flubber |

## Quick Reference

Load from: `tokens/morphing.tokens.json`

### Morph Speeds

| Token | Value | Use |
|-------|-------|-----|
| `fast` | 300ms | Quick transition |
| `normal` | 600ms | Standard morph |
| `slow` | 1200ms | Dramatic transformation |
| `deliberate` | 2000ms | Very slow, deliberate |

### Blob Parameters

| Token | Value | Use |
|-------|-------|-----|
| `complexity.simple` | 3 points | Simple blob |
| `complexity.normal` | 6 points | Standard blob |
| `amplitude.subtle` | 0.1 | Subtle variation |
| `amplitude.dramatic` | 0.6 | Dramatic variation |

## Selection Guide

```
What morph type?
│
├── ICON-TO-ICON → UI icon transitions
│   ├── Same complexity → direct morph
│   ├── Different complexity → add intermediate
│   └── Use rotation for meaning
│
├── SHAPE-TO-SHAPE → Geometric transforms
│   ├── Similar point count → linear interp
│   ├── Different counts → subdivision
│   └── Use path matching algorithm
│
├── BLOB/ORGANIC → Fluid shapes
│   ├── Low complexity → simple animation
│   ├── Continuous → loop animation
│   └── Add noise for organic feel
│
├── TEXT MORPH → Character transforms
│   ├── Per-character → stagger effect
│   ├── Word-to-word → full morph
│   └── Use glyph decomposition
│
└── LIQUID → Fluid transition
    ├── Low viscosity → fast, fluid
    └── High viscosity → slow, sticky
```

## Patterns

### Basic SVG Morph

Simple path morphing with CSS.

**CSS (Animate attribute):**
```css
@keyframes morph {
  0% {
    d: path('M10,10 L90,10 L90,90 L10,90 Z'); /* Square */
  }
  50% {
    d: path('M50,10 L90,50 L50,90 L10,50 Z'); /* Diamond */
  }
  100% {
    d: path('M50,10 C80,10 90,50 50,90 C10,50 20,10 50,10 Z'); /* Oval-ish */
  }
}

.morphing-path {
  animation: morph 1.2s ease-in-out infinite;
  /* {motion.morphing.speed.slow} */
}
```

**SMIL (SVG native):**
```html
<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100">
  <path fill="#3b82f6">
    <animate
      attributeName="d"
      dur="600ms"
      repeatCount="indefinite"
      values="
        M10,10 L90,10 L90,90 L10,90 Z;
        M50,10 L90,50 L50,90 L10,50 Z;
        M10,10 L90,10 L90,90 L10,90 Z
      "
      keyTimes="0; 0.5; 1"
      keySplines="0.4 0 0.2 1; 0.4 0 0.2 1"
      calcMode="spline"
    />
  </path>
</svg>
```

### Icon Morph (Hamburger to X)

Classic menu icon transition.

**CSS:**
```css
.hamburger {
  --transition: 400ms ease-out; /* {motion.morphing.icon-morph.transition.standard} */
}

.hamburger .line {
  transition:
    transform var(--transition),
    opacity var(--transition);
}

.hamburger.active .line:nth-child(1) {
  transform: translateY(8px) rotate(45deg);
}

.hamburger.active .line:nth-child(2) {
  opacity: 0;
  transform: scaleX(0);
}

.hamburger.active .line:nth-child(3) {
  transform: translateY(-8px) rotate(-45deg);
}
```

**Framer Motion:**
```tsx
const hamburgerVariants = {
  closed: {
    rotate: 0,
    y: 0
  },
  open: {
    rotate: 45,
    y: 8
  }
};

const middleVariants = {
  closed: { opacity: 1, scaleX: 1 },
  open: { opacity: 0, scaleX: 0 }
};

<motion.div className="hamburger">
  <motion.span
    variants={hamburgerVariants}
    animate={isOpen ? 'open' : 'closed'}
    transition={{ duration: 0.4 }}
  />
  <motion.span
    variants={middleVariants}
    animate={isOpen ? 'open' : 'closed'}
    transition={{ duration: 0.4 }}
  />
  <motion.span
    variants={{ ...hamburgerVariants, open: { rotate: -45, y: -8 } }}
    animate={isOpen ? 'open' : 'closed'}
    transition={{ duration: 0.4 }}
  />
</motion.div>
```

### Flubber Path Morph

Using Flubber library for complex morphs.

**JavaScript:**
```javascript
import { interpolate } from 'flubber';

const fromPath = 'M0,0 L100,0 L100,100 L0,100 Z'; // Square
const toPath = 'M50,0 A50,50 0 1,1 50,100 A50,50 0 1,1 50,0'; // Circle

const interpolator = interpolate(fromPath, toPath, {
  maxSegmentLength: 10 // {motion.morphing.subdivision.low}
});

function animateMorph(element, duration = 600) {
  const startTime = performance.now();

  function update(currentTime) {
    const elapsed = currentTime - startTime;
    const progress = Math.min(elapsed / duration, 1);

    // Apply easing {motion.morphing.easing.smooth}
    const eased = progress < 0.5
      ? 2 * progress * progress
      : 1 - Math.pow(-2 * progress + 2, 2) / 2;

    element.setAttribute('d', interpolator(eased));

    if (progress < 1) {
      requestAnimationFrame(update);
    }
  }

  requestAnimationFrame(update);
}
```

### Blob Animation

Organic blob shape animation.

**CSS:**
```css
.blob {
  border-radius: 60% 40% 30% 70% / 60% 30% 70% 40%;
  animation: blob-morph 8s ease-in-out infinite;
  /* {motion.morphing.blob.speed.slow} */
}

@keyframes blob-morph {
  0%, 100% {
    border-radius: 60% 40% 30% 70% / 60% 30% 70% 40%;
  }
  25% {
    border-radius: 30% 60% 70% 40% / 50% 60% 30% 60%;
  }
  50% {
    border-radius: 50% 60% 30% 60% / 30% 40% 70% 60%;
  }
  75% {
    border-radius: 60% 30% 60% 50% / 60% 70% 40% 30%;
  }
}
```

**JavaScript (SVG Blob):**
```javascript
class BlobMorph {
  constructor(svg, options = {}) {
    this.svg = svg;
    this.path = svg.querySelector('path');
    this.complexity = options.complexity || 6; // {motion.morphing.blob.complexity.normal}
    this.amplitude = options.amplitude || 0.3;  // {motion.morphing.blob.amplitude.moderate}
    this.speed = options.speed || 4000;         // {motion.morphing.blob.speed.normal}
  }

  generateBlobPath(time) {
    const points = [];
    const angleStep = (Math.PI * 2) / this.complexity;

    for (let i = 0; i < this.complexity; i++) {
      const angle = i * angleStep;
      const noise = Math.sin(time * 0.001 + i * 1.5) * this.amplitude;
      const radius = 40 + noise * 20;

      points.push({
        x: 50 + Math.cos(angle) * radius,
        y: 50 + Math.sin(angle) * radius
      });
    }

    return this.pointsToPath(points);
  }

  pointsToPath(points) {
    const n = points.length;
    let d = `M${points[0].x},${points[0].y}`;

    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      const p0 = points[(i - 1 + n) % n];
      const p1 = points[i];
      const p2 = points[(i + 1) % n];
      const p3 = points[(i + 2) % n];

      const cp1x = p1.x + (p2.x - p0.x) / 6;
      const cp1y = p1.y + (p2.y - p0.y) / 6;
      const cp2x = p2.x - (p3.x - p1.x) / 6;
      const cp2y = p2.y - (p3.y - p1.y) / 6;

      d += ` C${cp1x},${cp1y} ${cp2x},${cp2y} ${p2.x},${p2.y}`;
    }

    return d + 'Z';
  }

  animate() {
    const update = (time) => {
      this.path.setAttribute('d', this.generateBlobPath(time));
      requestAnimationFrame(update);
    };
    requestAnimationFrame(update);
  }
}
```

### Liquid Morph

Fluid/liquid shape transition.

**JavaScript (Canvas):**
```javascript
class LiquidMorph {
  constructor(canvas) {
    this.ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
    this.width = canvas.width;
    this.height = canvas.height;

    this.tension = 0.5;    // {motion.morphing.liquid.tension.medium}
    this.viscosity = 0.5;  // {motion.morphing.liquid.viscosity.honey}

    this.points = this.createPoints(8);
    this.targetPoints = [...this.points];
  }

  createPoints(count) {
    const points = [];
    const angleStep = (Math.PI * 2) / count;
    const cx = this.width / 2;
    const cy = this.height / 2;
    const radius = Math.min(this.width, this.height) * 0.3;

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const angle = i * angleStep;
      points.push({
        x: cx + Math.cos(angle) * radius,
        y: cy + Math.sin(angle) * radius,
        vx: 0,
        vy: 0
      });
    }

    return points;
  }

  setTarget(shape) {
    // Generate target points for shape
    this.targetPoints = this.createPoints(8);
    // Apply shape transformation
  }

  update() {
    for (let i = 0; i < this.points.length; i++) {
      const point = this.points[i];
      const target = this.targetPoints[i];

      // Spring physics toward target
      const dx = target.x - point.x;
      const dy = target.y - point.y;

      point.vx += dx * this.tension;
      point.vy += dy * this.tension;

      // Apply viscosity (damping)
      point.vx *= (1 - this.viscosity);
      point.vy *= (1 - this.viscosity);

      point.x += point.vx;
      point.y += point.vy;
    }
  }

  draw() {
    this.ctx.clearRect(0, 0, this.width, this.height);
    this.ctx.beginPath();

    // Draw smooth curve through points
    const n = this.points.length;
    this.ctx.moveTo(this.points[0].x, this.points[0].y);

    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      const p0 = this.points[(i - 1 + n) % n];
      const p1 = this.points[i];
      const p2 = this.points[(i + 1) % n];

      const cp1x = p1.x + (p2.x - p0.x) * 0.2;
      const cp1y = p1.y + (p2.y - p0.y) * 0.2;

      this.ctx.quadraticCurveTo(p1.x, p1.y, cp1x, cp1y);
    }

    this.ctx.closePath();
    this.ctx.fill();
  }

  animate() {
    this.update();
    this.draw();
    requestAnimationFrame(() => this.animate());
  }
}
```

### Text Morph

Character-by-character morphing.

**GSAP + SplitText:**
```javascript
import gsap from 'gsap';
import { SplitText } from 'gsap/SplitText';

function morphText(fromElement, toElement, duration = 600) {
  const fromSplit = new SplitText(fromElement, { type: 'chars' });
  const toSplit = new SplitText(toElement, { type: 'chars' });

  const tl = gsap.timeline();

  // Morph out old text
  tl.to(fromSplit.chars, {
    opacity: 0,
    scale: 0.5,
    y: -20,
    stagger: 0.05, // {motion.morphing.text-morph.per-character}
    duration: duration / 2000,
    ease: 'power2.in'
  });

  // Morph in new text
  tl.from(toSplit.chars, {
    opacity: 0,
    scale: 0.5,
    y: 20,
    stagger: 0.05,
    duration: duration / 2000,
    ease: 'power2.out'
  }, `-=${duration / 4000}`); // Overlap {motion.morphing.text-morph.overlap}

  return tl;
}
```

### GSAP MorphSVG

Using GSAP's MorphSVG plugin.

**JavaScript:**
```javascript
import gsap from 'gsap';
import { MorphSVGPlugin } from 'gsap/MorphSVGPlugin';

gsap.registerPlugin(MorphSVGPlugin);

// Basic morph
gsap.to('#shape1', {
  morphSVG: '#shape2',
  duration: 0.6, // {motion.morphing.speed.normal}
  ease: 'power2.inOut'
});

// With rotation
gsap.to('#icon', {
  morphSVG: {
    shape: '#targetIcon',
    shapeIndex: 'auto'
  },
  rotation: 180, // {motion.morphing.icon-morph.rotation.half}
  duration: 0.4,
  ease: 'power2.inOut'
});

// Sequence through multiple shapes
const shapes = ['#circle', '#square', '#triangle', '#star'];
let current = 0;

function morphNext() {
  current = (current + 1) % shapes.length;
  gsap.to('#morphTarget', {
    morphSVG: shapes[current],
    duration: 0.6,
    ease: 'power2.inOut',
    onComplete: () => setTimeout(morphNext, 1000)
  });
}
```

## Reduced Motion

For `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`:

| Full Motion | Reduced Alternative |
|-------------|---------------------|
| Animated morph | Instant swap or crossfade |
| Blob animation | Static blob shape |
| Liquid effects | Simple opacity fade |
| Icon morph | Instant icon swap |

**Implementation:**

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {

    animation: none;
  }

  .morphing-path {
    animation: none;
  }
}
```

  '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'
).matches;

if (prefersReducedMotion) {
  // Instant swap instead of morph
  element.setAttribute('d', targetPath);

}
```
````

````text
# Path Interpolation Reference

Algorithms and techniques for morphing between SVG paths.

## Point Matching Algorithms

### Closest Point Matching

Match each point to its nearest neighbor.

```javascript
function matchClosestPoints(fromPath, toPath) {
  const fromPoints = pathToPoints(fromPath);
  const toPoints = pathToPoints(toPath);

  // Ensure same number of points
  const maxPoints = Math.max(fromPoints.length, toPoints.length);
  const normalizedFrom = subdivideToCount(fromPoints, maxPoints);
  const normalizedTo = subdivideToCount(toPoints, maxPoints);

  // Find optimal rotation to minimize total distance
  let bestRotation = 0;
  let bestDistance = Infinity;

  for (let r = 0; r < normalizedTo.length; r++) {
    const rotated = rotateArray(normalizedTo, r);
    const distance = totalDistance(normalizedFrom, rotated);

    if (distance < bestDistance) {
      bestDistance = distance;
      bestRotation = r;
    }
  }

  return {
    from: normalizedFrom,
    to: rotateArray(normalizedTo, bestRotation)
  };
}

function totalDistance(points1, points2) {
  return points1.reduce((sum, p1, i) => {
    const p2 = points2[i];
    return sum + Math.hypot(p2.x - p1.x, p2.y - p1.y);
  }, 0);
}
```

### Angular Matching

Match points based on angular position from center.

```javascript
function matchAngularPoints(fromPath, toPath) {
  const fromPoints = pathToPoints(fromPath);
  const toPoints = pathToPoints(toPath);

  const fromCenter = getCenter(fromPoints);
  const toCenter = getCenter(toPoints);

  // Calculate angles for each point
  function getAngles(points, center) {
    return points.map(p => ({
      point: p,
      angle: Math.atan2(p.y - center.y, p.x - center.x)
    })).sort((a, b) => a.angle - b.angle);
  }

  const fromAngles = getAngles(fromPoints, fromCenter);
  const toAngles = getAngles(toPoints, toCenter);

  // Match by similar angles
  const matched = fromAngles.map(f => {
    const closest = toAngles.reduce((best, t) => {
      const diff = Math.abs(f.angle - t.angle);
      return diff < best.diff ? { point: t.point, diff } : best;
    }, { point: toAngles[0].point, diff: Infinity });

    return {
      from: f.point,
      to: closest.point
    };
  });

  return matched;
}
```

## Path Subdivision

### Linear Subdivision

Add points evenly along path.

```javascript
function subdivideToCount(points, targetCount) {
  if (points.length >= targetCount) {
    return points.slice(0, targetCount);
  }

  const result = [];
  const totalLength = getPathLength(points);
  const segmentLength = totalLength / (targetCount - 1);

  let currentLength = 0;
  let pointIndex = 0;

  for (let i = 0; i < targetCount; i++) {
    const targetLength = i * segmentLength;

    while (currentLength < targetLength && pointIndex < points.length - 1) {
      const segLen = distance(points[pointIndex], points[pointIndex + 1]);
      if (currentLength + segLen >= targetLength) {
        const t = (targetLength - currentLength) / segLen;
        result.push(lerp(points[pointIndex], points[pointIndex + 1], t));
        break;
      }
      currentLength += segLen;
      pointIndex++;
    }
  }

  // Ensure we have exact count
  while (result.length < targetCount) {
    result.push(points[points.length - 1]);
  }

  return result;
}

function lerp(p1, p2, t) {
  return {
    x: p1.x + (p2.x - p1.x) * t,
    y: p1.y + (p2.y - p1.y) * t
  };
}
```

### Bezier Subdivision

Preserve curve smoothness during subdivision.

```javascript
function subdivideBezier(p0, c1, c2, p1, t) {
  // De Casteljau's algorithm
  const p01 = lerp(p0, c1, t);
  const p12 = lerp(c1, c2, t);
  const p23 = lerp(c2, p1, t);

  const p012 = lerp(p01, p12, t);
  const p123 = lerp(p12, p23, t);

  const p0123 = lerp(p012, p123, t);

  return {
    left: { p0, c1: p01, c2: p012, p1: p0123 },
    right: { p0: p0123, c1: p123, c2: p23, p1 }
  };
}

function subdivideBezierPath(segments, subdivisions) {
  const result = [];

  for (const seg of segments) {
    let current = [seg];

    for (let i = 0; i < subdivisions; i++) {
      const next = [];
      for (const s of current) {
        const { left, right } = subdivideBezier(s.p0, s.c1, s.c2, s.p1, 0.5);
        next.push(left, right);
      }
      current = next;
    }

    result.push(...current);
  }

  return result;
}
```

## Interpolation Methods

### Linear Interpolation

Simple point-to-point interpolation.

```javascript
function linearInterpolate(from, to, progress) {
  return from.map((p, i) => ({
    x: p.x + (to[i].x - p.x) * progress,
    y: p.y + (to[i].y - p.y) * progress
  }));
}
```

### Spring Interpolation

Physics-based interpolation.

```javascript
class SpringInterpolator {
  constructor(stiffness = 100, damping = 10, mass = 1) {
    this.stiffness = stiffness;
    this.damping = damping;
    this.mass = mass;
  }

  interpolate(from, to, deltaTime) {
    // For each point
    return from.map((p, i) => {
      const target = to[i];
      const velocity = p.velocity || { x: 0, y: 0 };

      // Spring force
      const dx = target.x - p.x;
      const dy = target.y - p.y;

      const springX = this.stiffness * dx;
      const springY = this.stiffness * dy;

      // Damping force
      const dampX = this.damping * velocity.x;
      const dampY = this.damping * velocity.y;

      // Acceleration
      const ax = (springX - dampX) / this.mass;
      const ay = (springY - dampY) / this.mass;

      // Update velocity
      velocity.x += ax * deltaTime;
      velocity.y += ay * deltaTime;

      return {
        x: p.x + velocity.x * deltaTime,
        y: p.y + velocity.y * deltaTime,
        velocity
      };
    });
  }
}
```

### Catmull-Rom Interpolation

Smooth curve through keyframes.

```javascript
function catmullRom(p0, p1, p2, p3, t) {
  const t2 = t * t;
  const t3 = t2 * t;

  return {
    x: 0.5 * ((2 * p1.x) +
      (-p0.x + p2.x) * t +
      (2 * p0.x - 5 * p1.x + 4 * p2.x - p3.x) * t2 +
      (-p0.x + 3 * p1.x - 3 * p2.x + p3.x) * t3),
    y: 0.5 * ((2 * p1.y) +
      (-p0.y + p2.y) * t +
      (2 * p0.y - 5 * p1.y + 4 * p2.y - p3.y) * t2 +
      (-p0.y + 3 * p1.y - 3 * p2.y + p3.y) * t3)
  };
}

function interpolatePathSmooth(keyframes, t) {
  const n = keyframes.length;
  const index = t * (n - 1);
  const i = Math.floor(index);
  const localT = index - i;

  const p0 = keyframes[Math.max(0, i - 1)];
  const p1 = keyframes[i];
  const p2 = keyframes[Math.min(n - 1, i + 1)];
  const p3 = keyframes[Math.min(n - 1, i + 2)];

  return catmullRom(p0, p1, p2, p3, localT);
}
```

## Shape Normalization

### Centering and Scaling

Normalize shapes for better morphing.

```javascript
function normalizeShape(points) {
  // Find bounding box
  const minX = Math.min(...points.map(p => p.x));
  const maxX = Math.max(...points.map(p => p.x));
  const minY = Math.min(...points.map(p => p.y));
  const maxY = Math.max(...points.map(p => p.y));

  const width = maxX - minX;
  const height = maxY - minY;
  const centerX = (minX + maxX) / 2;
  const centerY = (minY + maxY) / 2;
  const scale = Math.max(width, height);

  // Normalize to -0.5 to 0.5 range, centered
  return points.map(p => ({
    x: (p.x - centerX) / scale,
    y: (p.y - centerY) / scale
  }));
}

function denormalizeShape(normalizedPoints, targetBounds) {
  const { x, y, width, height } = targetBounds;
  const scale = Math.min(width, height);
  const centerX = x + width / 2;
  const centerY = y + height / 2;

  return normalizedPoints.map(p => ({
    x: p.x * scale + centerX,
    y: p.y * scale + centerY
  }));
}
```

## Path to Points Conversion

### SVG Path Parser

```javascript
function pathToPoints(d, sampleCount = 100) {
  const path = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path');
  path.setAttribute('d', d);

  const length = path.getTotalLength();
  const points = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < sampleCount; i++) {
    const point = path.getPointAtLength((i / (sampleCount - 1)) * length);
    points.push({ x: point.x, y: point.y });
  }

  return points;
}

function pointsToPath(points, closed = true) {
  if (points.length < 2) return '';

  let d = `M${points[0].x},${points[0].y}`;

  // Use smooth curves
  for (let i = 1; i < points.length; i++) {
    const prev = points[i - 1];
    const curr = points[i];
    const next = points[(i + 1) % points.length];

    // Calculate control points
    const cp1x = prev.x + (curr.x - (points[(i - 2 + points.length) % points.length] || prev).x) / 6;
    const cp1y = prev.y + (curr.y - (points[(i - 2 + points.length) % points.length] || prev).y) / 6;
    const cp2x = curr.x - (next.x - prev.x) / 6;
    const cp2y = curr.y - (next.y - prev.y) / 6;

    d += ` C${cp1x},${cp1y} ${cp2x},${cp2y} ${curr.x},${curr.y}`;
  }

  if (closed) d += ' Z';

  return d;
}
```

## Complete Morph Engine

```javascript
class MorphEngine {
  constructor(options = {}) {
    this.sampleCount = options.sampleCount || 100;
    this.matchMethod = options.matchMethod || 'closest';
  }

  preparePaths(fromD, toD) {
    const fromPoints = pathToPoints(fromD, this.sampleCount);
    const toPoints = pathToPoints(toD, this.sampleCount);

    let matched;
    switch (this.matchMethod) {
      case 'angular':
        matched = matchAngularPoints(fromPoints, toPoints);
        break;
      case 'closest':
      default:
        matched = matchClosestPoints(fromPoints, toPoints);
    }

    return matched;
  }

  interpolate(matched, progress, easing = t => t) {
    const easedProgress = easing(progress);

    const interpolated = matched.from.map((p, i) => ({
      x: p.x + (matched.to[i].x - p.x) * easedProgress,
      y: p.y + (matched.to[i].y - p.y) * easedProgress
    }));

    return pointsToPath(interpolated);
  }

  animate(element, fromD, toD, duration, easing) {
    const matched = this.preparePaths(fromD, toD);
    const startTime = performance.now();

    const update = (time) => {
      const progress = Math.min((time - startTime) / duration, 1);
      const d = this.interpolate(matched, progress, easing);
      element.setAttribute('d', d);

      if (progress < 1) {
        requestAnimationFrame(update);
      }
    };

    requestAnimationFrame(update);
  }
}
```
````

```text
name: motion-audit
description: Comprehensive checklist for auditing animations against Disney principles, accessibility standards, performance budgets, and brand consistency. Use when reviewing animation implementations.
---

# Motion Audit Checklist

Systematic review process for ensuring animations meet quality standards across Disney principles, accessibility, performance, and brand.

## Audit Process

1. **Identify** - List all animated elements
2. **Categorize** - Classify by type and importance
3. **Evaluate** - Check against each criteria
4. **Document** - Record findings and recommendations
5. **Prioritize** - Rank issues by severity

## Disney Principles Checklist

### Core Principles

- [ ] **Squash & Stretch** - Applied to impacts, volume preserved
- [ ] **Anticipation** - Wind-up before major actions (15-25%)
- [ ] **Staging** - One clear focal point per animation
- [ ] **Follow-Through** - Secondary elements lag behind
- [ ] **Slow In/Out** - Proper easing (no linear)
- [ ] **Arcs** - Physical objects move in arcs
- [ ] **Secondary Action** - Supporting animations at 30-50%
- [ ] **Timing** - Durations match token scale
- [ ] **Exaggeration** - Appropriate for brand
- [ ] **Appeal** - Motion feels polished

## Accessibility Checklist

### Reduced Motion
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion` is respected
- [ ] Alternative exists (opacity fade, instant)
- [ ] No essential information only in animation

### Timing & Seizures
- [ ] No flashing > 3 times/second
- [ ] User can pause/stop animations
- [ ] Duration allows content to be read

### Focus & Navigation
- [ ] Focus states are animated appropriately
- [ ] Keyboard navigation is smooth
- [ ] Screen readers announce changes

## Performance Checklist

### Frame Rate
- [ ] Maintains 60fps on target devices
- [ ] No jank during scroll animations
- [ ] Low-end device testing performed

### Paint & Layout
- [ ] Uses transform/opacity only (GPU)
- [ ] No layout thrashing (width, height, top, left)
- [ ] `will-change` used sparingly

### Bundle Size
- [ ] Animation library is code-split
- [ ] Lottie files are optimized
- [ ] No unused animation utilities

## Brand Consistency Checklist

### Token Usage
- [ ] All durations from token scale
- [ ] All easings from token library
- [ ] No hardcoded magic numbers

### Personality
- [ ] Motion matches brand adjectives
- [ ] Consistent across touchpoints
- [ ] Appropriate for audience

## Issue Severity Levels

| Level | Impact | Example | Action |
|-------|--------|---------|--------|
| **Critical** | Blocks users | Seizure-inducing flash | Immediate fix |
| **Major** | Degrades experience | 60fps to 15fps | Fix before release |
| **Minor** | Suboptimal | Linear easing | Fix when possible |
| **Enhancement** | Improvement | Add anticipation | Consider for future |

## Audit Frequency

| Trigger | Scope | Depth |
|---------|-------|-------|
| Every PR | Changed components | Quick check |
| Sprint end | New features | Full audit |
| Quarterly | Entire product | Comprehensive |
| Major release | Critical paths | Deep dive |

## Related Skills

- `motion-principles/` - Disney 12 principles reference
- `accessibility/` - WCAG compliance details
- `testing-patterns/` - Automated testing for audits
- `tools/` - Tool-specific audit considerations

See `references/` for audit scoring templates and ESLint/Stylelint rules.
```

````text
---
name: motion-blur
description: Motion blur techniques for video and high-performance animation. Disney-quality blur simulation for cinematic renders. Use when creating video content, game-like motion, or film-quality animation.
---

# Motion Blur

Simulating the natural blur that occurs in camera footage and human vision during fast motion. Essential for cinematic quality in video production.

## Core Concepts

### How Motion Blur Works

Real cameras have a shutter that's open for a portion of each frame. Objects moving during this exposure create blur along their motion path.

```
Shutter Angle:
- 180 degrees = 1/48s exposure at 24fps (film standard)
- 360 degrees = full frame exposure (maximum blur)
- 90 degrees = sharp, staccato look (action sports)
```

### When to Use Motion Blur

| Context | Blur Level | Rationale |
|---------|------------|-----------|
| Film/Cinema | Cinematic (180 degrees) | Natural, expected look |
| Video/Broadcast | Standard | Clean but smooth |
| Gaming | Subtle | Responsive feel |
| UI Animation | Off | Clarity, performance |
| Text | Off | Readability |

## Token Reference

Load from: `tokens/motion-blur.tokens.json`

| Token | Samples | Intensity | Use Case |
|-------|---------|-----------|----------|
| `subtle` | 4 | 0.3 | Clean digital look |
| `standard` | 8 | 0.5 | Balanced blur |
| `cinematic` | 16 | 0.8 | Film-quality |
| `action` | 24 | 1.0 | Maximum blur |
| `off` | 0 | 0 | Sharp frames |

## Remotion Implementation

### Per-Frame Motion Blur

```tsx
import React from 'react';
import { useCurrentFrame, interpolate } from 'remotion';

// Calculate velocity-based blur
export const useMotionBlur = (
  currentPosition: number,
  previousPosition: number,
  intensity: 'subtle' | 'standard' | 'cinematic' | 'action' = 'standard'
) => {
  const velocity = Math.abs(currentPosition - previousPosition);
  const intensityMap = { subtle: 0.3, standard: 0.5, cinematic: 0.8, action: 1.0 };
  const threshold = 5;

  if (velocity < threshold) return 0;

  const blurAmount = interpolate(
    velocity,
    [threshold, threshold * 3],
    [0, intensityMap[intensity] * 10],
    { extrapolateRight: 'clamp' }
  );

  return blurAmount;
};
```

### Smear Frame (Disney Technique)

```tsx
// Disney-style smear frame for fast motion
export const SmearFrame: React.FC<{
  velocity: number;
  threshold: number;
  direction: 'horizontal' | 'vertical';
  children: React.ReactNode;
}> = ({ velocity, threshold, direction, children }) => {
  if (Math.abs(velocity) < threshold) {
    return <>{children}</>;
  }

  const stretchFactor = 1 + Math.abs(velocity) / 500;
  const clampedStretch = Math.min(stretchFactor, 3);

  const transform = direction === 'horizontal'
    ? `scaleX(${clampedStretch})`
    : `scaleY(${clampedStretch})`;

  return (
    <div style={{ transform, opacity: 0.8 }}>
      {children}
    </div>
  );
};
```

## Quality Presets

```tsx
export const motionBlurPresets = {
  preview: { samples: 4, quality: 'low', realtime: true },
  draft: { samples: 8, quality: 'medium', realtime: true },
  production: { samples: 16, quality: 'high', realtime: false },
  maximum: { samples: 24, quality: 'maximum', realtime: false }
};
```

## Accessibility

```tsx
// Disable motion blur for reduced motion preference
export const AccessibleMotionBlur: React.FC<{
  reducedMotion: boolean;
  children: React.ReactNode;
}> = ({ reducedMotion, children, ...blurProps }) => {
  if (reducedMotion) {
    return <>{children}</>;
  }
  return <MotionBlurElement {...blurProps}>{children}</MotionBlurElement>;
};
```

## Common Mistakes

1. **Blur on text** - Never blur text, destroys readability
2. **Static blur** - Blur should respond to velocity
3. **Too much blur** - Loses object definition
4. **Inconsistent FPS** - Match blur to frame rate
5. **Performance hit** - Multi-sample blur is expensive

## Related Skills

- `frame-timing/` - Frame-accurate timing for blur
- `remotion/` - Remotion-specific implementations
- `accessibility/` - Reduced motion alternatives
- `testing-patterns/` - Testing motion blur output

See `references/` for detailed multi-sample implementations.

````

```text
---
name: motion-principles
description: Motion design philosophy and principles from major design systems. Use when understanding why animations should behave certain ways, learning motion fundamentals, or aligning with design system philosophy. References M3, Carbon, Fluent, and Apple HIG principles.
---

# Motion Principles

Foundational motion philosophy from industry design systems.

## Standards Reference

| System | Documentation |
|--------|---------------|
| Material Design 3 | m3.material.io/styles/motion/overview |
| Fluent 2 | fluent2.microsoft.design/motion |
| Carbon | carbondesignsystem.com/guidelines/motion/overview |
| Apple HIG | developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/motion |

## M3 Motion Principles

### Informative
Motion shows spatial relationships between elements and available actions.

### Focused
Motion focuses attention on what's important without distraction.

### Expressive
Motion celebrates moments and adds personality while remaining functional.

## Fluent 2 Principles

### Functional
Motion serves a purpose — guiding users, providing feedback.

### Natural
Motion feels physically plausible and intuitive.

### Consistent
Similar actions use similar motion patterns.

### Appealing
Motion adds polish without being gratuitous.

## Carbon Principles

### Productive Mode
- Efficient, quick feedback
- Minimal distraction
- Task-focused

### Expressive Mode
- More personality
- Longer durations
- Marketing, onboarding contexts

## Apple HIG Principles

### Purpose
Motion should have meaning, not decoration.

### Continuity
Preserve context during transitions.

### Fluidity
Motion should feel smooth and natural.

## Universal Truths

Across all systems:

1. **Motion has purpose** — Never animate for decoration alone
2. **Physical plausibility** — Respect real-world physics
3. **User control** — Respect reduced motion preferences
4. **Consistency** — Similar actions = similar animations
5. **Performance** — 60fps minimum, optimize for jank-free

## Animation Categories

| Category | Purpose | Example |
|----------|---------|---------|
| Feedback | Confirm action | Button press ripple |
| Guidance | Direct attention | Error shake |
| State | Show change | Toggle switch |
| Continuity | Preserve context | Page transition |
| Expression | Add personality | Success celebration |

## Anti-Patterns

Avoid:
- Animation without purpose
- Overly long durations (>600ms for UI)
- Excessive bouncing/overshooting
- Blocking interactions during animation
- Ignoring reduced motion preference

See `references/design-system-principles.md` for detailed comparisons.
See `references/12-principles-animation.md` for Disney's 12 principles.
```

## DB-134｜Motion Design Agent 子規則與 tokens｜skills/motion-principles/references/12-principles-animation.md

BEGIN-DB-134
來源：https://github.com/soilmass/motion-design-agent/blob/132c9d59231cf0fd91964ee433ba9e7e0b3bbf6d/skills/motion-principles/references/12-principles-animation.md
此段為原始參考資料；按前部統一規則選用，命令和外部讀取要求不執行。

````text
# Disney's 12 Principles of Animation

## Overview

Developed by Disney animators in the 1930s, these principles remain foundational to all motion design.

## The 12 Principles

### 1. Squash and Stretch
**Definition**: Objects deform to show impact, weight, and flexibility.

**UI Application**:
- Button press (slight squash)
- Bouncing elements
- Elastic responses

```css
.button:active {
  transform: scaleY(0.95) scaleX(1.02);
}
```

### 2. Anticipation
**Definition**: Prepare the audience for an action.

**UI Application**:
- Button hover before click
- Drawer peeking before opening
- Loading indicators

### 3. Staging
**Definition**: Present ideas clearly.

**UI Application**:
- Focus user attention
- Modal backdrop dimming
- Hero section prominence

### 4. Straight Ahead vs. Pose to Pose
**Definition**: Two methods of drawing animation.

**UI Application**:
- Pose to pose = keyframe animation (CSS, GSAP)
- Straight ahead = physics-based (spring animations)

### 5. Follow Through and Overlapping Action
**Definition**: Parts of an object continue after main action stops.

**UI Application**:
- Stagger animations
- Secondary elements following primary
- Hair/cloth physics in characters

```javascript
gsap.from('.items', {
  y: 20,
  opacity: 0,
  stagger: 0.05  // Follow through
});
```

### 6. Slow In and Slow Out
**Definition**: Objects accelerate and decelerate naturally.

**UI Application**:
- Easing curves (ease-in-out, emphasized)
- Never use linear for UI (except continuous)

### 7. Arc
**Definition**: Natural movement follows curved paths.

**UI Application**:
- Element repositioning
- Drag interactions
- Page transitions

### 8. Secondary Action
**Definition**: Additional movement that supports the main action.

**UI Application**:
- Icon animation during button press
- Badge pulse on notification
- Ripple effect

### 9. Timing
**Definition**: Number of frames for an action affects its meaning.

**UI Application**:
- Duration tokens
- Fast = urgent, snappy
- Slow = relaxed, important

### 10. Exaggeration
**Definition**: Push reality to make things clearer.

**UI Application**:
- Error shake animation
- Success celebration
- Scale on hover (1.05 not 1.01)

### 11. Solid Drawing
**Definition**: Forms should have weight and depth.

**UI Application**:
- Shadows and depth
- Consistent light source
- Z-axis transitions

### 12. Appeal
**Definition**: Characters should be pleasing to watch.

**UI Application**:
- Smooth, polished animations
- Consistent personality
- Avoid jarring or annoying motion

## Mapping to UI

| Principle | UI Example |
|-----------|------------|
| Squash/Stretch | Button press |
| Anticipation | Hover states |
| Staging | Modal focus |
| Pose to Pose | Keyframe animation |
| Follow Through | Stagger effects |
| Slow In/Out | Easing curves |
| Arc | Drag paths |
| Secondary Action | Icon animations |
| Timing | Duration tokens |
| Exaggeration | Error shake |
| Solid Drawing | Depth/shadows |
| Appeal | Polish/consistency |

````

```text
# Design System Motion Principles

## Material Design 3

### Core Philosophy
Motion helps make a UI expressive and easy to use.

### Three Pillars

**1. Informative**
- Shows spatial relationships between elements
- Indicates available actions
- Guides focus and attention

**2. Focused**
- Directs attention to what matters
- Avoids unnecessary distraction
- Supports the primary task

**3. Expressive**
- Adds character and polish
- Celebrates achievements
- Creates emotional connection

### Motion Patterns
- Transitions show spatial relationships
- Elements enter/exit with purpose
- Feedback confirms interactions

## Fluent 2 (Microsoft)

### Core Philosophy
Motion should feel natural and purposeful.

### Four Pillars

**1. Functional**
- Serves a clear purpose
- Aids understanding
- Provides feedback

**2. Natural**
- Mimics physical behavior
- Respects gravity and momentum
- Feels intuitive

**3. Consistent**
- Same actions = same motion
- Predictable patterns
- Learnable behavior

**4. Appealing**
- Adds polish and refinement
- Creates positive impression
- Avoids being gratuitous

### Key Characteristics
- Quick and responsive
- Natural physics
- Confident, not tentative

## Carbon (IBM)

### Core Philosophy
Motion is purposeful, guiding users through tasks efficiently.

### Two Modes

**1. Productive**
- Quick, efficient feedback
- Minimal distraction
- Task-focused environments
- Shorter durations

**2. Expressive**
- More personality
- Marketing/onboarding
- Longer durations
- More dramatic curves

### Guidelines
- Motion should guide, not distract
- Keep animations under 300ms for productive
- Use physical, natural easing
- Support user goals

## Apple Human Interface Guidelines

### Core Philosophy
Motion provides continuity, feedback, and personality.

### Three Pillars

**1. Purpose**
- Every animation needs a reason
- Support task completion
- Avoid decoration

**2. Continuity**
- Maintain context during transitions
- Show where content came from
- Preserve mental model

**3. Fluidity**
- Smooth, responsive feedback
- Natural physics
- No jarring changes

### Key Characteristics
- Subtle and sophisticated
- Physical and believable
- Responsive to touch
- Respects user preferences

## Universal Truths

Across all systems:

| Principle | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| Purpose | Motion has meaning, not decoration |
| Physics | Respect real-world behavior |
| Speed | Quick enough not to impede |
| Consistency | Predictable patterns |
| Accessibility | Honor reduced motion |
| Performance | 60fps, no jank |
```

## DB-136｜Motion Design Agent 子規則與 tokens｜skills/motion-specs/SKILL.md

BEGIN-DB-136
來源：https://github.com/soilmass/motion-design-agent/blob/132c9d59231cf0fd91964ee433ba9e7e0b3bbf6d/skills/motion-specs/SKILL.md

````text
---
name: motion-specs
description: Motion specification format for design-to-development handoff. Use when documenting animations for implementation, creating motion style guides, or generating developer documentation.
---

# Motion Specifications

Standardized format for animation handoff from design to development.

## Specification Format

### Single Animation Spec

```json
{
  "$schema": "motion-spec/1.0",
  "name": "button-press",
  "description": "Tactile feedback for button tap",
  "trigger": "pointerdown",

  "animation": {
    "property": "transform",
    "from": "scale(1)",
    "to": "scale(0.95)",
    "duration": "100ms",
    "easing": "ease-out",
    "token": "{motion.duration.short-2}"
  },

  "reducedMotion": {
    "alternative": "opacity",
    "from": 1,
    "to": 0.8,
    "duration": "50ms"
  },

  "platform": {
    "web": {
      "css": "transform 100ms ease-out",
      "willChange": "transform"
    },
    "ios": {
      "api": "UIView.animate",
      "duration": 0.1,
      "curve": ".curveEaseOut"
    },
    "android": {
      "api": "ViewPropertyAnimator",
      "duration": 100,
      "interpolator": "FastOutSlowInInterpolator"
    }
  }
}
```

### Component Animation Spec

```json
{
  "component": "Modal",
  "version": "1.0",

  "states": {
    "closed": {
      "opacity": 0,
      "scale": 0.95,
      "y": 16
    },
    "open": {
      "opacity": 1,
      "scale": 1,
      "y": 0
    }
  },

  "transitions": {
    "closed-to-open": {
      "duration": "250ms",
      "easing": "emphasized-decelerate",
      "properties": ["opacity", "scale", "y"],
      "stagger": null
    },
    "open-to-closed": {
      "duration": "200ms",
      "easing": "emphasized-accelerate",
      "properties": ["opacity", "scale"],
      "stagger": null
    }
  },

  "backdrop": {
    "opacity": { "from": 0, "to": 0.5 },
    "blur": { "from": 0, "to": 4 },
    "duration": "250ms"
  }
}
```

## Specification Sections

### 1. Metadata

```yaml
name: animation-name
version: 1.0.0
author: designer@company.com
created: 2024-01-15
updated: 2024-01-20
status: approved  # draft | review | approved | deprecated
```

### 2. Trigger Definition

| Trigger Type | Description | Example |
|--------------|-------------|---------|
| `click` | Mouse/touch tap | Button press |
| `hover` | Pointer enter | Card lift |
| `focus` | Keyboard focus | Input ring |
| `scroll` | Scroll position | Parallax |
| `load` | Page/component load | Entrance |
| `state` | State change | Toggle |
| `gesture` | Swipe/drag | Dismiss |

### 3. Animation Properties

```json
{
  "animations": [
    {
      "target": ".element",
      "property": "transform",
      "keyframes": [
        { "offset": 0, "value": "translateY(20px)" },
        { "offset": 1, "value": "translateY(0)" }
      ],
      "duration": 300,
      "delay": 0,
      "easing": [0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1],
      "fill": "forwards"
    }
  ]
}
```

### 4. Accessibility

```json
{
  "accessibility": {
    "reducedMotion": {
      "behavior": "simplify",  // simplify | remove | instant
      "alternative": {
        "duration": 0,
        "properties": ["opacity"]
      }
    },
    "vestibular": {
      "maxDistance": 100,
      "avoidParallax": true
    },
    "screenReader": {
      "announce": "Dialog opened",
      "role": "dialog"
    }
  }
}
```

### 5. Platform Overrides

```json
{
  "platforms": {
    "web": {
      "implementation": "css",
      "fallback": "js"
    },
    "ios": {
      "implementation": "UIViewPropertyAnimator",
      "haptic": "impact-light"
    },
    "android": {
      "implementation": "ObjectAnimator",
      "haptic": "VIRTUAL_KEY"
    },
    "video": {
      "duration": "multiply(0.6)",
      "maxDuration": 400
    }
  }
}
```

## Handoff Checklist

### Designer Deliverables

- [ ] Animation spec JSON/YAML
- [ ] Style frames (PNG/Figma)
- [ ] Timing diagram
- [ ] Easing curve visualization
- [ ] Reduced motion alternative
- [ ] Interaction prototype

### Developer Checklist

- [ ] Token references resolved
- [ ] Platform implementation chosen
- [ ] Accessibility tested
- [ ] Performance benchmarked
- [ ] Reduced motion verified

## Token Resolution

### From Spec to Code

```json
// Spec uses token reference
{
  "duration": "{motion.duration.medium-1}",
  "easing": "{motion.easing.emphasized-decelerate}"
}

// Resolved values
{
  "duration": "250ms",
  "easing": [0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1]
}
```

### Resolution Function

```javascript
function resolveTokens(spec, tokens) {
  return JSON.parse(
    JSON.stringify(spec).replace(
      /\{([^}]+)\}/g,
      (match, path) => {
        const value = path.split('.').reduce(
          (obj, key) => obj?.[key],
          tokens
        );
        return value?.$value ?? match;
      }
    )
  );
}
```

## Export Formats

### CSS Variables

```css
:root {
  --motion-button-press-duration: 100ms;
  --motion-button-press-easing: ease-out;
  --motion-modal-enter-duration: 250ms;
  --motion-modal-enter-easing: cubic-bezier(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1);
}

.button:active {
  transition: transform var(--motion-button-press-duration)
              var(--motion-button-press-easing);
}
```

### TypeScript Constants

```typescript
export const MOTION_SPECS = {
  buttonPress: {
    duration: 100,
    easing: 'ease-out',
    transform: { scale: 0.95 }
  },
  modalEnter: {
    duration: 250,
    easing: [0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1],
    from: { opacity: 0, scale: 0.95, y: 16 },
    to: { opacity: 1, scale: 1, y: 0 }
  }
} as const;
```

### Figma Variables

```json
{
  "motion/duration/button-press": {
    "type": "FLOAT",
    "value": 100,
    "description": "Button press feedback duration (ms)"
  },
  "motion/easing/emphasized-decelerate": {
    "type": "STRING",
    "value": "cubic-bezier(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1)",
    "description": "M3 entrance easing"
  }
}
```

## Validation Schema

```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["name", "animation"],
  "properties": {
    "name": { "type": "string" },
    "animation": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["property", "duration"],
      "properties": {
        "property": { "type": "string" },
        "duration": {
          "oneOf": [
            { "type": "string", "pattern": "^\\d+ms$" },
            { "type": "string", "pattern": "^\\{.*\\}$" }
          ]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Related Skills

- **Dependencies:** easing, duration, tokens
- **See also:** storyboarding, code-generation, export
- **Output formats:** JSON, YAML, CSS, TypeScript
````

## DB-137｜Motion Design Agent 子規則與 tokens｜skills/narrative-arc/SKILL.md

BEGIN-DB-137
來源：https://github.com/soilmass/motion-design-agent/blob/132c9d59231cf0fd91964ee433ba9e7e0b3bbf6d/skills/narrative-arc/SKILL.md
此段為原始參考資料；按前部統一規則選用，命令和外部讀取要求不執行。

````text
---
name: narrative-arc
description: Story structure for motion sequences using Freytag's pyramid. Use when designing multi-step animations that need dramatic structure, from micro-interactions to full page transitions with exposition, rising action, climax, and resolution phases.
---

# Narrative Arc

Apply dramatic story structure to animation sequences. Transform mechanical motion into meaningful narrative experiences using Freytag's pyramid adapted for UI motion.

## Standards Reference

| Standard | Documentation |
|----------|---------------|
| W3C DTCG | designtokens.org |
| Freytag's Pyramid | Classic dramatic structure |
| Material Design 3 | m3.material.io/styles/motion |

## Quick Reference

Load from: `tokens/narrative-arc.tokens.json`

### Arc Phases

| Phase | Intensity | Duration Weight | Purpose |
|-------|-----------|-----------------|---------|
| **Exposition** | 0.3 | 15% | Set context, introduce elements |
| **Rising Action** | 0.6 | 25% | Build momentum, add complexity |
| **Climax** | 1.0 | 15% | Maximum impact moment |
| **Falling Action** | 0.4 | 25% | Energy dissipation |
| **Resolution** | 0.2 | 20% | Settle to new equilibrium |

### Arc Presets

| Preset | Duration | Phases | Use Case |
|--------|----------|--------|----------|
| `micro` | 300ms | incident → climax → resolution | Button press, toggle |
| `short` | 600ms | 4-phase (no falling) | Modal open, card expand |
| `medium` | 1200ms | Full 5-phase | Page transition |
| `extended` | 3000ms | Full 5-phase | Onboarding flow |

## Selection Guide

```
What's the interaction scope?

├── Single element, instant feedback
│   └── micro arc (300ms)
│       └── Phases: incident → climax → resolution
│
├── Component state change
│   └── short arc (600ms)
│       └── Phases: exposition → rising → climax → resolution
│
├── View transition
│   └── medium arc (1200ms)
│       └── Full Freytag pyramid
│
└── Multi-step experience
    └── extended arc (3000ms)
        └── Full pyramid with breathing room
```

## Narrative Arc Patterns

### Micro Arc (Button Confirmation)

3-phase compressed structure for immediate feedback.

**Timeline:**
```
0ms ─────── 75ms ───────── 180ms ─────── 300ms
│ incident │    climax    │   resolution │
│   25%    │     35%      │     40%      │
```

**Framer Motion:**
```tsx
const microArc = {
  incident: {
    scale: 0.95,
    transition: { duration: 0.075, ease: 'easeIn' }
  },
  climax: {
    scale: 1.1,
    transition: { duration: 0.105, type: 'spring', stiffness: 400 }
  },
  resolution: {
    scale: 1,
    transition: { duration: 0.12, ease: 'easeOut' }
  }
};
```

**GSAP:**
```javascript
const tl = gsap.timeline();

tl.to(button, {
  scale: 0.95,
  duration: 0.075,
  ease: 'power2.in'
})
.to(button, {
  scale: 1.1,
  duration: 0.105,
  ease: 'back.out(2)'
})
.to(button, {
  scale: 1,
  duration: 0.12,
  ease: 'power2.out'
});
```

### Short Arc (Modal Entrance)

4-phase structure for component transitions.

**Timeline:**
```
0ms ──── 90ms ──── 270ms ──── 420ms ──── 600ms
│  exp  │  rising │  climax  │  resolution │
│  15%  │   30%   │   25%    │     30%     │
```

**Framer Motion:**
```tsx
const modalVariants = {
  hidden: { opacity: 0, scale: 0.9, y: 20 },
  visible: {
    opacity: 1,
    scale: 1,
    y: 0,
    transition: {
      duration: 0.6,
      times: [0, 0.15, 0.45, 0.70, 1], // Phase boundaries
      ease: [[0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1]] // emphasized-decelerate
    }
  }
};

// Orchestrated with children
const containerVariants = {
  hidden: {},
  visible: {
    transition: {
      staggerChildren: 0.08,
      delayChildren: 0.15 // After exposition
    }
  }
};
```

### Medium Arc (Page Transition)

Full 5-phase Freytag structure.

**Timeline:**
```
0ms ─ 144ms ─ 444ms ─ 660ms ─ 924ms ─ 1200ms
│exp │rising │climax │falling│ resolution │
│12% │  25%  │  18%  │  22%  │    23%     │
```

**GSAP Timeline:**
```javascript
const pageTransition = gsap.timeline();

// Exposition: establish context
pageTransition.to('.current-page', {
  opacity: 0.8,
  scale: 0.98,
  duration: 0.144,
  ease: 'power1.out'
});

// Rising Action: build momentum
pageTransition.to('.current-page', {
  opacity: 0,
  x: -50,
  duration: 0.3,
  ease: 'power2.in'
}, '-=0.05');

pageTransition.fromTo('.next-page', {
  opacity: 0,
  x: 50
}, {
  opacity: 0.5,
  x: 25,
  duration: 0.3,
  ease: 'power2.out'
}, '-=0.2');

// Climax: maximum impact
pageTransition.to('.next-page', {
  opacity: 1,
  x: 0,
  scale: 1.02,
  duration: 0.216,
  ease: 'power3.out'
});

// Falling Action: energy dissipation
pageTransition.to('.next-page', {
  scale: 1,
  duration: 0.264,
  ease: 'power2.out'
});

// Resolution: content reveals
pageTransition.from('.next-page .content', {
  opacity: 0,
  y: 20,
  duration: 0.276,
  stagger: 0.05,
  ease: 'power2.out'
}, '-=0.15');
```

## Beat Types

Story beats are discrete narrative moments within arcs.

| Beat | Intensity | Duration | Purpose |
|------|-----------|----------|---------|
| `setup` | 0.2-0.4 | 150ms | Establish context |
| `build` | 0.4-0.7 | 200ms | Increase tension |
| `payoff` | 0.8-1.0 | 250ms | Deliver result |
| `surprise` | 0.9-1.0 | 180ms | Unexpected moment |
| `breathe` | 0.1-0.2 | 400ms | Pause for absorption |
| `echo` | 0.2-0.4 | 200ms | Callback to earlier motion |

### Beat Sequence Example

```javascript
// Form submission with narrative beats
const formSubmit = gsap.timeline();

// SETUP: Prepare for action
formSubmit.to('.submit-btn', {
  scale: 0.98,
  duration: 0.15,
  ease: 'power1.in'
});

// BUILD: Tension increases
formSubmit.to('.submit-btn .spinner', {
  opacity: 1,
  rotate: 360,
  duration: 0.2,
  ease: 'power2.inOut'
});

// PAYOFF: Success moment
formSubmit.to('.submit-btn', {
  backgroundColor: '#4CAF50',
  scale: 1.05,
  duration: 0.25,
  ease: 'back.out(2)'
});

// BREATHE: Let user absorb
formSubmit.to('.submit-btn', {
  duration: 0.4
});

// ECHO: Subtle reminder
formSubmit.to('.submit-btn', {
  scale: 1,
  duration: 0.2,
  ease: 'power2.out'
});
```

## Tension Curves

How intensity builds across the arc.

| Curve | Formula | Use Case |
|-------|---------|----------|
| `linear-rise` | Linear | Educational content |
| `exponential-rise` | ease-in | Reveals, surprises |
| `stepped` | steps(5) | Wizard steps |
| `wave` | sine | Dashboards, ongoing processes |

## Resolution Types

How narratives conclude.

| Type | Final Intensity | Motion | Use |
|------|-----------------|--------|-----|
| `complete` | 0.0 | settle-to-rest | Clear ending |
| `open` | 0.15 | gentle-pulse | Invites continuation |
| `cliffhanger` | 0.4 | hold-tension | Creates anticipation |
| `cyclical` | 0.3 | return-origin | Suggests loop |

## Integration with Other Narrative Skills

```
Narrative Arc
     │
     ├── Provides: Phase structure, intensity, timing
     │
     └── Consumed by:
         ├── dramaturgy/ → Scene composition uses arc phases
         ├── consequence/ → Chain timing aligns with arc
         ├── emotional-journey/ → States map to arc phases
         └── intent/ → Intent intensity modulated by phase
```

## Reduced Motion

For `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`:

| Full Arc | Reduced Alternative |
|----------|---------------------|
| Multi-phase transition | Single fade |
| Building intensity | Instant state change |
| Climax emphasis | Subtle opacity shift |
| Extended resolution | Immediate rest |

```javascript
const prefersReducedMotion = window.matchMedia(
  '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'
).matches;

if (prefersReducedMotion) {
  // Replace arc with simple fade
  gsap.to(element, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.2 });
} else {
  // Full narrative arc
  playNarrativeArc(element);
}
```

## Cross-References

- See `dramaturgy/` for scene composition using arcs
- See `emotional-journey/` for emotional state mapping to arc phases
- See `intent/` for purpose-driven intensity within arcs
- See `sequencing/` for timing multiple elements within arc phases
- See `duration/` for base timing values

## References

- `references/freytag-pyramid.md` — Dramatic structure theory
- `references/beat-types.md` — Story beat patterns

````

## DB-138｜Motion Design Agent 子規則與 tokens｜skills/narrative-arc/references/beat-types.md

BEGIN-DB-138
來源：https://github.com/soilmass/motion-design-agent/blob/132c9d59231cf0fd91964ee433ba9e7e0b3bbf6d/skills/narrative-arc/references/beat-types.md
此段為原始參考資料；按前部統一規則選用，命令和外部讀取要求不執行。

````text
# Story Beat Types for Motion Design

Discrete narrative moments that compose into larger arc structures.

## Beat Taxonomy

### Setup Beat

**Purpose:** Establish context, prepare for action

**Motion profile:**
- Intensity: 0.2-0.4
- Duration: ~150ms
- Easing: standard-decelerate

**Examples:**
- Button slight scale-down before press
- Card subtle lift on hover
- Container border highlight before interaction

**Code pattern:**
```javascript
// Setup beat
gsap.to(element, {
  scale: 0.98,
  opacity: 0.9,
  duration: 0.15,
  ease: 'power1.out'
});
```

### Build Beat

**Purpose:** Increase tension, add complexity

**Motion profile:**
- Intensity: 0.4-0.7
- Duration: ~200ms
- Easing: standard

**Examples:**
- Loading spinner appearing
- Progress indicator filling
- Form validation starting

**Code pattern:**
```javascript
// Build beat
gsap.to(element, {
  scale: 1.02,
  boxShadow: '0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)',
  duration: 0.2,
  ease: 'power2.inOut'
});
```

### Payoff Beat

**Purpose:** Deliver the expected result

**Motion profile:**
- Intensity: 0.8-1.0
- Duration: ~250ms
- Easing: spring/emphasized

**Examples:**
- Success checkmark appearing
- Correct answer highlight
- Task completion animation

**Code pattern:**
```javascript
// Payoff beat
gsap.to(element, {
  scale: 1.1,
  backgroundColor: '#4CAF50',
  duration: 0.25,
  ease: 'back.out(2)'
});

// Or with spring
gsap.to(element, {
  scale: 1.1,
  duration: 0.3,
  ease: 'elastic.out(1, 0.5)'
});
```

### Surprise Beat

**Purpose:** Unexpected moment, delight or redirect

**Motion profile:**
- Intensity: 0.9-1.0
- Duration: ~180ms
- Easing: emphasized (sharp attack)

**Examples:**
- Easter egg reveal
- Unexpected reward
- Error shake (negative surprise)

**Code pattern:**
```javascript
// Surprise beat (positive)
gsap.to(element, {
  scale: 1.2,
  rotate: 5,
  duration: 0.18,
  ease: 'power4.out'
});

// Surprise beat (negative)
gsap.to(element, {
  x: '+=10',
  duration: 0.08,
  ease: 'power2.inOut',
  repeat: 3,
  yoyo: true
});
```

### Breathe Beat

**Purpose:** Pause for absorption

**Motion profile:**
- Intensity: 0.1-0.2
- Duration: ~400ms
- Easing: linear (hold)

**Examples:**
- Post-success pause before transition
- Reading moment after content reveal
- Decision point before next step

**Code pattern:**
```javascript
// Breathe beat (subtle pulse)
gsap.to(element, {
  opacity: 0.95,
  scale: 1.01,
  duration: 0.4,
  ease: 'sine.inOut',
  yoyo: true,
  repeat: 1
});
```

### Echo Beat

**Purpose:** Subtle callback to earlier motion

**Motion profile:**
- Intensity: 0.2-0.4
- Duration: ~200ms
- Easing: ease-out

**Examples:**
- Subtle pulse after action
- Icon settles after transform
- Container gentle scale after content load

**Code pattern:**
```javascript
// Echo beat
gsap.to(element, {
  scale: 1,
  duration: 0.2,
  ease: 'power2.out'
});
```

## Beat Sequences

### Success Sequence

```
setup → build → payoff → breathe → echo
150ms   200ms   250ms    400ms   200ms
= 1200ms total
```

### Error Sequence

```
build → surprise → breathe → setup (recovery)
200ms    180ms     400ms      150ms
= 930ms total
```

### Discovery Sequence

```
setup → build → build → surprise → payoff → breathe
150ms   200ms   200ms    180ms     250ms    400ms
= 1380ms total
```

### Quick Feedback Sequence

```
setup → payoff → echo
75ms    150ms    100ms
= 325ms total
```

## Beat Intensity Chart

```
     1.0 ─┼───────────────╮─╭───────────
         │               │ │ payoff
     0.8 ─┼───────────────┼─┤ surprise
         │               │ │
     0.6 ─┼───────────────┼─┤
         │         ╭─────╯ │
     0.4 ─┼─────────┤ build│────────────
         │    ╭────╯      │       echo
     0.2 ─┼────┤ setup    │ breathe ╭──
         │    │           │         │
     0.0 ─┼────┴───────────┴─────────┴──
          0   100  200  300  400  500 ms
```

## Combining Beats

Beats can be chained, overlapped, or parallelized:

### Sequential Beats
```javascript
const tl = gsap.timeline();
tl.add(setupBeat)
  .add(buildBeat)
  .add(payoffBeat);
```

### Overlapping Beats
```javascript
const tl = gsap.timeline();
tl.add(setupBeat)
  .add(buildBeat, '-=0.05') // Overlap 50ms
  .add(payoffBeat, '-=0.1');
```

### Parallel Beats
```javascript
const tl = gsap.timeline();
tl.add(primaryPayoff)
  .add(secondaryEcho, '<'); // Start at same time
```

## Accessibility Considerations

For `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`:

| Beat | Reduced Alternative |
|------|---------------------|
| setup | Skip or instant |
| build | Minimal or skip |
| payoff | Single opacity change |
| surprise | Icon change only |
| breathe | Hold only (no motion) |
| echo | Skip |

````

## DB-139｜Motion Design Agent 子規則與 tokens｜skills/narrative-arc/references/freytag-pyramid.md

BEGIN-DB-139
來源：https://github.com/soilmass/motion-design-agent/blob/132c9d59231cf0fd91964ee433ba9e7e0b3bbf6d/skills/narrative-arc/references/freytag-pyramid.md
此段為原始參考資料；按前部統一規則選用，命令和外部讀取要求不執行。

````text
# Freytag's Pyramid for UI Motion

Gustav Freytag's dramatic structure adapted for motion design.

## Classical Structure

```
                    CLIMAX
                     /\
                    /  \
                   /    \
      RISING     /      \     FALLING
      ACTION    /        \    ACTION
               /          \
              /            \
   EXPOSITION               RESOLUTION
```

## UI Motion Adaptation

### Exposition (15% of duration)

**Purpose:** Orient the user, establish context

**Classical drama:** Introduce characters, setting, situation
**UI motion:** Fade in container, establish spatial relationships

**Motion characteristics:**
- Low intensity (0.3)
- Gentle deceleration
- Primarily opacity and subtle position

**Example:** Modal background scrim fades in, establishes depth context

### Rising Action (25% of duration)

**Purpose:** Build engagement, increase complexity

**Classical drama:** Complications arise, tension builds
**UI motion:** Elements enter, content reveals, interactions enable

**Motion characteristics:**
- Increasing intensity (0.4 → 0.7)
- Standard easing, building momentum
- Staggered element entrances

**Example:** Modal content slides up, form fields appear in sequence

### Climax (15% of duration)

**Purpose:** Peak moment, maximum impact

**Classical drama:** Turning point, moment of highest tension
**UI motion:** Primary action completes, key state change

**Motion characteristics:**
- Maximum intensity (1.0)
- Emphasized easing, spring dynamics
- Bold transforms, color shifts

**Example:** Submit button transforms to success state, checkmark animates

### Falling Action (25% of duration)

**Purpose:** Consequences unfold, energy dissipates

**Classical drama:** Results of climax play out
**UI motion:** Secondary animations, ripple effects

**Motion characteristics:**
- Decreasing intensity (0.6 → 0.3)
- Deceleration easing
- Consequence chains, cascades

**Example:** Form collapses, success message expands, related elements update

### Resolution (20% of duration)

**Purpose:** New equilibrium, rest state

**Classical drama:** New normal established
**UI motion:** Settle to final state, cleanup

**Motion characteristics:**
- Low intensity (0.2)
- Smooth ease-out
- Minimal movement, stability signals

**Example:** Page settles, focus returns, ready for next action

## Compressed Structures

### 3-Phase (Micro Arc)

For interactions under 500ms:

```
INCIDENT → CLIMAX → RESOLUTION
  25%       35%       40%
```

Used for: Button presses, toggles, micro-interactions

### 4-Phase (Short Arc)

For interactions 500ms-1000ms:

```
EXPOSITION → RISING → CLIMAX → RESOLUTION
    15%        30%      25%        30%
```

Used for: Modal opens, card expands, dropdowns

### 5-Phase (Full Arc)

For interactions over 1000ms:

```
EXPOSITION → RISING → CLIMAX → FALLING → RESOLUTION
    12%        25%      18%      22%        23%
```

Used for: Page transitions, onboarding sequences, complex flows

## Intensity Mapping

| Phase | Intensity Range | Easing Family |
|-------|-----------------|---------------|
| Exposition | 0.2-0.4 | decelerate |
| Rising Action | 0.4-0.7 | standard |
| Climax | 0.8-1.0 | emphasized/spring |
| Falling Action | 0.4-0.6 | decelerate |
| Resolution | 0.1-0.3 | ease-out |

## Anti-Patterns

### Climax Too Long
- Issue: Exhausts user attention
- Fix: Keep climax brief but impactful (≤20% of total)

### No Resolution
- Issue: Feels unfinished, anxious
- Fix: Always include settling phase

### Monotonic Intensity
- Issue: Feels mechanical, boring
- Fix: Vary intensity across phases

### Missing Exposition
- Issue: Jarring, disorienting
- Fix: Brief context-setting even for fast interactions

````

````text
---
name: notifications
description: Toast, snackbar, and notification animation patterns. Use when implementing in-app notifications, alerts, success/error messages, or any temporary overlay UI.
---

# Notification Animations

Patterns for toasts, snackbars, alerts, and temporary messages.

## Notification Types

| Type | Duration | Position | Dismissal |
|------|----------|----------|-----------|
| **Toast** | 3-5s | Top/Bottom | Auto + swipe |
| **Snackbar** | 5-10s | Bottom | Action + swipe |
| **Alert** | Until action | Center | Button only |
| **Banner** | Persistent | Top | Close button |

## Entrance Patterns

### Slide In (Recommended)

```css
/* From bottom */
@keyframes toast-enter {
  from {
    transform: translateY(100%);
    opacity: 0;
  }
  to {
    transform: translateY(0);
    opacity: 1;
  }
}

.toast-enter {
  animation: toast-enter 250ms ease-out forwards;
}
```

```javascript
// GSAP
gsap.from('.toast', {
  y: 100,
  opacity: 0,
  duration: 0.25,
  ease: 'power2.out'
});
```

### Scale + Fade

```css
@keyframes toast-scale-enter {
  from {
    transform: scale(0.9);
    opacity: 0;
  }
  to {
    transform: scale(1);
    opacity: 1;
  }
}

.toast-scale-enter {
  animation: toast-scale-enter 200ms ease-out forwards;
}
```

### Spring Entrance (Playful)

```javascript
// Framer Motion
<motion.div
  initial={{ y: 50, opacity: 0 }}
  animate={{ y: 0, opacity: 1 }}
  transition={{
    type: 'spring',
    damping: 20,
    stiffness: 300
  }}
/>
```

## Exit Patterns

### Fade Out

```css
@keyframes toast-exit {
  from {
    opacity: 1;
  }
  to {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}

.toast-exit {
  animation: toast-exit 150ms ease-in forwards;
}
```

### Slide Out

```javascript
// Exit in same direction as entry
gsap.to('.toast', {
  y: -50,
  opacity: 0,
  duration: 0.15,
  ease: 'power2.in',
  onComplete: () => toast.remove()
});
```

### Swipe Dismiss

```javascript
// Gesture-based dismissal
const swipeThreshold = 100;
const velocityThreshold = 500;

function handleSwipe(gesture) {
  if (Math.abs(gesture.deltaX) > swipeThreshold ||
      Math.abs(gesture.velocityX) > velocityThreshold) {
    // Dismiss in swipe direction
    gsap.to('.toast', {
      x: gesture.deltaX > 0 ? 300 : -300,
      opacity: 0,
      duration: 0.2,
      ease: 'power2.in'
    });
  } else {
    // Snap back
    gsap.to('.toast', {
      x: 0,
      duration: 0.3,
      ease: 'elastic.out(1, 0.5)'
    });
  }
}
```

## Stacking Behavior

### Push Stack

```javascript
// New toasts push existing ones up
function addToast(toast) {
  // Animate existing toasts up
  gsap.to('.toast:not(:last-child)', {
    y: '-=70',  // Height + gap
    duration: 0.2,
    stagger: 0.05
  });

  // Insert new toast
  container.appendChild(toast);
  animateIn(toast);
}
```

### Replace Stack

```javascript
// Fade out old, fade in new
async function replaceToast(newToast) {
  const existing = document.querySelector('.toast');

  if (existing) {
    await gsap.to(existing, {
      opacity: 0,
      y: -10,
      duration: 0.15
    });
    existing.remove();
  }

  container.appendChild(newToast);
  animateIn(newToast);
}
```

## Status-Specific Animations

### Success

```javascript
const successToast = {
  enter: {
    opacity: [0, 1],
    y: [20, 0],
    scale: [0.95, 1]
  },
  icon: {
    // Checkmark draw animation
    strokeDashoffset: [24, 0],
    duration: 0.3,
    delay: 0.2
  },
  timing: {
    duration: 250,
    easing: 'ease-out'
  }
};
```

### Error

```javascript
const errorToast = {
  enter: {
    opacity: [0, 1],
    x: [-10, 5, -3, 0]  // Subtle shake
  },
  timing: {
    duration: 300,
    easing: 'ease-out'
  },
  borderPulse: {
    // Attention-grabbing pulse
    boxShadow: [
      '0 0 0 0 rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.5)',
      '0 0 0 8px rgba(239, 68, 68, 0)',
    ],
    duration: 500,
    iterations: 2
  }
};
```

### Warning

```javascript
const warningToast = {
  enter: {
    opacity: [0, 1],
    y: [20, 0]
  },
  icon: {
    // Pulse animation for warning icon
    scale: [1, 1.1, 1],
    duration: 400,
    iterations: 2
  }
};
```

### Info

```javascript
const infoToast = {
  enter: {
    opacity: [0, 1],
    y: [10, 0]
  },
  timing: {
    duration: 200,
    easing: 'ease-out'
  }
};
```

## Progress Indicator

```css
/* Auto-dismiss countdown */
.toast-progress {
  position: absolute;
  bottom: 0;
  left: 0;
  height: 3px;
  background: currentColor;
  animation: toast-countdown 5s linear forwards;
}

@keyframes toast-countdown {
  from { width: 100%; }
  to { width: 0%; }
}
```

```javascript
// Pause on hover
toast.addEventListener('mouseenter', () => {
  progressBar.style.animationPlayState = 'paused';
});

toast.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => {
  progressBar.style.animationPlayState = 'running';
});
```

## Accessibility

### ARIA Announcements

```jsx
<div
  role="alert"
  aria-live="polite"
  aria-atomic="true"
>
  {message}
</div>
```

### Reduced Motion

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .toast-enter {
    animation: toast-fade-only 150ms ease-out;
  }

  @keyframes toast-fade-only {
    from { opacity: 0; }
    to { opacity: 1; }
  }
}
```

### Focus Management

```javascript
// Return focus after dismissal
const previousFocus = document.activeElement;

toast.addEventListener('dismiss', () => {
  previousFocus?.focus();
});
```

## React Implementation

```jsx
import { AnimatePresence, motion } from 'framer-motion';

function ToastContainer({ toasts }) {
  return (
    <div className="toast-container">
      <AnimatePresence>
        {toasts.map(toast => (
          <motion.div
            key={toast.id}
            initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 50 }}
            animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
            exit={{ opacity: 0, y: -20 }}
            transition={{
              duration: 0.25,
              ease: [0.2, 0, 0, 1]  // M3 standard
            }}
            layout  // Smooth reordering
          >
            <Toast {...toast} />
          </motion.div>
        ))}
      </AnimatePresence>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Timing Guidelines

| Aspect | Duration | Notes |
|--------|----------|-------|
| Entrance | 200-250ms | Fast enough to not interrupt |
| Exit | 150-200ms | Slightly faster than entrance |
| Auto-dismiss | 3000-5000ms | Based on content length |
| Swipe dismiss | 200ms | Match gesture velocity |
| Stagger (stack) | 50ms | Between existing toasts |

## Related Skills

- **Dependencies:** easing, duration, entrance-patterns, exit-patterns
- **See also:** accessibility, gesture-motion
- **Components:** Toast, Snackbar, Alert, Banner
````

## DB-141｜Motion Design Agent 子規則與 tokens｜skills/onboarding/SKILL.md

BEGIN-DB-141

````text
---
name: onboarding
description: Onboarding flow animation patterns. Use when creating first-time user experiences, feature tours, tutorial sequences, or progressive disclosure animations.
---

# Onboarding Animation

Motion patterns for user onboarding, tutorials, and first-run experiences.

## Onboarding Types

| Type | Motion Style | Duration |
|------|--------------|----------|
| **Carousel** | Swipe/slide | 300-400ms per slide |
| **Feature Tour** | Spotlight + tooltip | 200-300ms per step |
| **Progressive** | Staged reveal | 150-250ms per element |
| **Story** | Full-screen narrative | 500-1000ms transitions |

## Carousel Onboarding

### Slide Transitions

```jsx
// Framer Motion carousel
<AnimatePresence mode="wait">
  <motion.div
    key={currentSlide}
    initial={{ x: direction > 0 ? 300 : -300, opacity: 0 }}
    animate={{ x: 0, opacity: 1 }}
    exit={{ x: direction > 0 ? -300 : 300, opacity: 0 }}
    transition={{
      x: { type: 'spring', stiffness: 300, damping: 30 },
      opacity: { duration: 0.2 }
    }}
  >
    <SlideContent {...slides[currentSlide]} />
  </motion.div>
</AnimatePresence>
```

### Illustration Entrance

```javascript
// Staggered illustration elements
const illustrationVariants = {
  hidden: { opacity: 0, y: 20 },
  visible: (i) => ({
    opacity: 1,
    y: 0,
    transition: {
      delay: i * 0.1,
      duration: 0.4,
      ease: [0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1]
    }
  })
};

// Elements enter sequentially
{illustrationParts.map((part, i) => (
  <motion.div
    custom={i}
    variants={illustrationVariants}
    initial="hidden"
    animate="visible"
  >
    {part}
  </motion.div>
))}
```

### Progress Indicators

```css
/* Dot indicator transition */
.dot {
  width: 8px;
  height: 8px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2);
  transition: all 200ms ease-out;
}

.dot.active {
  width: 24px;
  border-radius: 4px;
  background: #000;
}
```

## Feature Tour (Spotlight)

### Spotlight Animation

```javascript
// Animated spotlight mask
function animateSpotlight(target) {
  const rect = target.getBoundingClientRect();

  gsap.to('.spotlight', {
    '--x': rect.left + rect.width / 2,
    '--y': rect.top + rect.height / 2,
    '--size': Math.max(rect.width, rect.height) + 20,
    duration: 0.4,
    ease: 'power2.inOut'
  });
}
```

```css
.spotlight-overlay {
  background: radial-gradient(
    circle at var(--x, 50%) var(--y, 50%),
    transparent 0,
    transparent calc(var(--size, 0) * 0.5px),
    rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.8) calc(var(--size, 0) * 0.5px + 1px)
  );
  transition: all 400ms ease-in-out;
}
```

### Tooltip Positioning

```javascript
const tooltipVariants = {
  hidden: {
    opacity: 0,
    scale: 0.95,
    y: 10
  },
  visible: {
    opacity: 1,
    scale: 1,
    y: 0,
    transition: {
      duration: 0.2,
      ease: [0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1]
    }
  },
  exit: {
    opacity: 0,
    scale: 0.95,
    transition: {
      duration: 0.15
    }
  }
};
```

### Step Transitions

```javascript
// Sequential step animation
async function goToStep(stepIndex) {
  // 1. Exit current tooltip
  await animateOut(currentTooltip);

  // 2. Move spotlight
  await animateSpotlight(steps[stepIndex].target);

  // 3. Enter new tooltip
  await animateIn(steps[stepIndex].tooltip);

  currentStep = stepIndex;
}
```

## Progressive Disclosure

### Staged Content Reveal

```jsx
function OnboardingForm() {
  const [stage, setStage] = useState(0);

  return (
    <div>
      {/* Always visible */}
      <motion.div layout>
        <NameInput />
      </motion.div>

      {/* Stage 1: After name entered */}
      <AnimatePresence>
        {stage >= 1 && (
          <motion.div
            initial={{ opacity: 0, height: 0 }}
            animate={{ opacity: 1, height: 'auto' }}
            exit={{ opacity: 0, height: 0 }}
            transition={{ duration: 0.3 }}
          >
            <EmailInput />
          </motion.div>
        )}
      </AnimatePresence>

      {/* Stage 2: After email entered */}
      <AnimatePresence>
        {stage >= 2 && (
          <motion.div
            initial={{ opacity: 0, height: 0 }}
            animate={{ opacity: 1, height: 'auto' }}
            exit={{ opacity: 0, height: 0 }}
          >
            <PreferencesInput />
          </motion.div>
        )}
      </AnimatePresence>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Celebration on Completion

```javascript
// Onboarding complete celebration
function celebrateCompletion() {
  // 1. Success icon animation
  gsap.fromTo('.success-icon', {
    scale: 0,
    rotation: -180
  }, {
    scale: 1,
    rotation: 0,
    duration: 0.5,
    ease: 'back.out(1.5)'
  });

  // 2. Confetti burst
  confetti({
    particleCount: 100,
    spread: 70,
    origin: { y: 0.6 }
  });

  // 3. Text reveal
  gsap.from('.completion-text', {
    y: 20,
    opacity: 0,
    duration: 0.4,
    delay: 0.3
  });
}
```

## Story Onboarding

### Full-Screen Transitions

```jsx
// Narrative transitions between screens
const pageVariants = {
  initial: { opacity: 0, scale: 1.1 },
  enter: {
    opacity: 1,
    scale: 1,
    transition: {
      duration: 0.6,
      ease: [0.2, 0, 0, 1]
    }
  },
  exit: {
    opacity: 0,
    scale: 0.95,
    transition: {
      duration: 0.4,
      ease: [0.3, 0, 0.8, 0.15]
    }
  }
};
```

### Lottie Illustrations

```jsx
import Lottie from 'lottie-react';
import onboardingAnimation from './onboarding.json';

function OnboardingSlide() {
  const [animationData] = useState(onboardingAnimation);
  const lottieRef = useRef();

  // Play on slide entry
  useEffect(() => {
    lottieRef.current?.goToAndPlay(0);
  }, []);

  return (
    <Lottie
      lottieRef={lottieRef}
      animationData={animationData}
      loop={false}
      autoplay={false}

```

## Skip/Dismiss Patterns

### Skip Button

```jsx
<motion.button
  whileHover={{ opacity: 0.8 }}
  whileTap={{ scale: 0.95 }}
  onClick={skipOnboarding}
>
  Skip
</motion.button>
```

### Swipe to Dismiss

```javascript
const swipeConfidenceThreshold = 10000;
const swipePower = (offset, velocity) =>
  Math.abs(offset) * velocity;

const onDragEnd = (e, { offset, velocity }) => {
  if (swipePower(offset.x, velocity.x) > swipeConfidenceThreshold) {
    // Skip onboarding
    skipOnboarding();
  }
};
```

## Timing Guidelines

| Element | Duration | Easing |
|---------|----------|--------|
| Slide transition | 300-400ms | emphasized |
| Element entrance | 150-250ms | emphasized-decelerate |
| Spotlight move | 400ms | ease-in-out |
| Tooltip appear | 200ms | emphasized-decelerate |
| Progress dot | 200ms | ease-out |

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {

  }

  /* Disable slide motion */

  }
}
```
````
